title: The Higher Court
corpus_scope: 56,736 meta-reviewer units (90% from 2024–26) · 6,547 borderline 2026 panels · association, not cause
question: What does the area chair weigh differently from the panel it summarizes, and what does the bench forgive at the margin?

figures.title: Two grammars: what the panel inspects, what the chair weighs
figures.deck: The chair does not re-litigate evidence — it weighs verdicts: statistics, positioning, novelty.

claims.statement: 56,736 meta-reviewer units, nine tenths of them from 2024–26, joined at the margin to 6,547 borderline 2026 panels.
claims.derivation: raw count of extracted meta-review logic units, n = 56,736 (PANEL.meta.meta_reviewer.n)

claims.statement: Statistics and metrics grow from 10% of reviewer attention to 26% of the chair's, related work from 5% to 16%, novelty doubles — the objects a chair can rule on from the reviews alone.
claims.derivation: COURT.grammars.reviewer.objects[o].share vs. COURT.grammars.ac.objects[o].share, for o in {stats_metrics, related_work, novelty}, across 952,856 official-reviewer units and 56,736 meta-reviewer units

claims.statement: Empirical scope, theory, and method design — the objects that demand re-reading the paper — fall to less than half their reviewer share.
claims.derivation: COURT.grammars.ac.objects[o].share ÷ COURT.grammars.reviewer.objects[o].share < 0.5 for o in {empirical_scope, theory, method_design}

figures.title: What the bench forgives at the margin
figures.deck: At the margin, only a clarity charge reliably blocks the pardon.

claims.statement: Clarity's interval clears zero — a paper the panel found hard to read is 4.4 points less likely to be lifted.
claims.derivation: COURT.forgive.clarity.adj_delta, matched inside 0.25-point mean-rating bins among the 6,547 borderline 2026 panels, 95% interval from resampling whole papers excludes zero

claims.statement: Identity charges (framing, novelty) lean against the lift.
claims.derivation: sign of COURT.forgive[o].adj_delta is negative for o in {problem_framing, novelty}

claims.statement: Robustness and related-work charges are the ones the bench most readily overlooks.
claims.derivation: COURT.forgive[o].adj_delta most positive (paper still lifted despite the charge) for o in {robustness_sensitivity, related_work}

figures.title: The redemption: what the chair praises when it lifts a paper
figures.deck: 75% of a lifted paper's meta-review is praise — of its numbers and its positioning; on rejected borderline papers, praise falls to 8%.

claims.statement: Roughly three-quarters of a lifted paper's meta-review is praise, favoring its numbers and its positioning; on a rejected borderline paper, praise of any kind nearly vanishes.
claims.derivation: COURT.redemption praise-share of meta-review units on lifted vs. rejected borderline papers

caveats.text: These comparisons are association, not cause: the accept line and the borderline band are inferred from outcomes, and a paper's fate may hinge on information the panel mean does not carry — a chair's own reading, a scope policy, a discounted reviewer.
The meta-review is written by the area chair after the decision is already made, so its praise reflects the language of justification, not independent evidence of paper quality.
